# A, owing 500.00 USD, refilled with 1,000.00 USD from C — more than it owes.
#
# A goes from −500.00 to +500.00. So 500.00 of the refill repays what A owes,
# drawing down A's owed cost basis at 1.35 and C's held one at 1.30, and the
# other 500.00 moves within the held side from C to A, drawing down no cost
# basis and opening none. C's cost basis falls by the 500.00 the held side
# lost, not by the 1,000.00 C sent.
#
# C's 1,000.00 is valued at the 1.30 it cost, 1,300.00, and A's 1,000.00 at the
# 500.00 repaid at 1.35, 675.00, plus the 500.00 moved at 1.30, 650.00.
# `$residual$` takes the 25.00 realized on repaying at 1.35 a debt with dollars
# that cost 1.30.
#
# Imported into the book usd_moved_out_of_an_empty_account.txt makes.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_a_balance_past_zero_has_a_cost_basis_on_the_other_side.py.
2034-02-01 * "Refill A with 1,000.00 USD from C"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:USD C -1000.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "13/10"
		value: "-1300.00"
		cost_basis_split_guid: "0a0a0000000000000000000000000003"
	Assets:USD A 1000.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "53/40"
		value: "1325.00"
		cost_basis_split_guid: "0a0a0000000000000000000000000001"
	Income:FX Gain $residual$ CAD
